about: Build queue. Work the 'ready' items top to bottom without re-asking the owner; they are decided. 'blocked' items wait on what 'blocked_on' says. When an item is done, delete it here and add a 'done' entry to progress.json (replacing its 'planned' entry if it has one).

items.title: Test mode: Test Panel, /wftest commands and a Play guide
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: a test mode with a clickable Test Panel plus matching commands, covering spawn/army, base/mana, siege and player tools; delivered the easiest private way.
spec: Build this first: the owner wants to start playtesting.

Server: /wftest on|off (permission level 2, so singleplayer with cheats on or an opped player). A per-player test-mode flag (attachment). Every action below is one server method, reached both by a /wftest subcommand and by a C2S payload from the panel; the server re-checks the flag and permission on every payload.

Client: F8 (rebindable KeyMapping) opens the Test Panel when test mode is on. Tabs: Spawn, Base, Siege, Player. Plain clean dark panels now; switch to the ui-foundation theme when that lands (don't wait for it).

Spawn tab: race, role, count (1-10), friendly (yours, joins your army) or enemy (pick faction); spawns in front of the player. War beasts (ignores beastLimit in test mode). Army buttons: heal all, kill all, dismiss all. Rank picker and 'revive all heroes' appear once veterancy and fallen-heroes exist.

Base tab: set base level 1-5 (a test override stored on the base, shown as 'TEST' in /army and later the War Table); fill all mana networks within 32 blocks; infinite-mana toggle for those networks; 'starter base' places a Mana Well, two Pylons, a Summoning Altar, a War Standard and an Arrow Tower in a clear flat spot in front of the player.
Siege tab: start a wave now from any enemy faction at the nearest War Standard; jump to wave N; pause/resume; end the siege. Raise/destroy outpost appears once siege-outposts exists.

Player tab: switch race (same as /warfront race, no cooldown); fill souls, rage, glider durability (and later rocket fuel, spell mana); set day / night / clear weather; god mode (invulnerable + creative-style flight toggle); give a kit of every Warfront item for the current race.
Buttons for features not built yet are shown greyed with 'coming'. Standing rule: every later feature adds its own Test Panel controls and /wftest subcommand (recorded in CLAUDE.md).
Game tests: each /wftest subcommand does its job (spawn count, base level override, mana filled, wave started); a player without test mode can't use the payloads.

Codex: a new 'Play' page: (1) install the Modrinth App, (2) download warfront-modpack from the latest green Actions run (GitHub, signed in), unzip it to get Warfront-Age-of-Banners.mrpack, (3) Modrinth App: Add instance -> From file -> pick it, give it 6+ GB RAM, Play. Then: make a creative or cheats-on world, /wftest on, press F8. Plain words, a screenshot-style step list.

items.title: The advisor: first-hour guide and quest line
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: one villain in seven disguises is each race's advisor, runs the tutorial, is revealed after the hidden warlord falls (who was trying to stop him), and is fought in the End with only your heroes and beasts against a mixed army.
spec: An advisor NPC per player (non-hostile, invulnerable, can't be pushed or led), appearing at the player's first base after they pick a race (or at spawn until they have one). Seven disguises: a robed elder in each race's colors (human court wizard, elf seer, dwarf runekeeper, orc shaman, demon whisperer, angel oracle, Hive synapse-elder). Placeholder looks until the owner designs them.
Never hint at the twist in-game; a few lines can be read differently once you know (write them that way).

First-hour quest line, one step at a time with a short line from the advisor and a toast: pick a race; place a Mana Well; plant Manabloom and harvest a shard; build the Summoning Altar; summon 3 troops; plant a War Standard; survive your first raid. Each step gives a small reward (shards, a crystal, a starter tower). Progress saved on the player; skippable with a config option or by talking to him and choosing 'I know the way'.
Afterwards: right-click him for hints about the next thing to unlock (base level, towers, warlords), war news (which faction's war meter is highest), and the nudge to march when a War Map drops.
Uses toasts and the ui-foundation theme for his lines when that exists; plain chat-style lines until then.
Test Panel: jump to any quest step; respawn the advisor; switch his disguise.
Game tests: completing a step advances the quest; skipping works; the advisor can't be hurt.

items.title: Difficulty presets, raid scaling, pacing and the recall home
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: Easy/Normal/Hard/Warlord presets; raids scale with base level and war meter; calm 3-day start then a steady beat; raids come even when you're away, with a warning timer and a teleport home.
spec: Preset per world (saved data; chosen with a small screen on first join or defaulting to Normal; changeable with /wftest difficulty and the Test Panel). Multipliers (config): Easy raid size x0.7, enemy health/damage x0.8, raids ~1 per 1.5 days; Normal x1 / x1 / ~1 per day; Hard x1.4 / x1.25 / ~1.3 per day; Warlord x1.8 / x1.5 / ~1.5 per day, and fallen heroes are lost for good (no revive, no altar return).

Raid strength = base size for the base level (levels 1-5) + a bonus per point of that faction's war meter, times the preset. Army size and ranks are ignored. Applies to warbands, sieges, outposts and fortress defenders.
Grace period: no warbands or sieges in the first 3 in-game days of a world (config), or until the advisor quest reaches 'plant a War Standard', whichever comes later.

Rhythm: replace the flat 5-minute warband roll and nightly siege roll with a raid scheduler per player: about one raid per in-game day (time of day random), a siege every 3-4 nights, at least one quiet day in every three. Faction picked by campaign-wars' mixed random rule.

Other dimensions (owner, 2026-10-07): while the player is in a dimension other than their base's, the raid scheduler runs at half speed (config 'awayDimensionRaidRate' 0.5), so there's time to explore the Nether, Aether, Otherside and other mods' worlds. Sieges already due still come with the warning and recall.
Warning: every base raid is announced 2 minutes ahead (toast + siege banner + horn sound) with a countdown on the HUD, wherever the player is, any dimension.

Recall home: during the warning and the raid, the player can teleport to their War Standard (button on the warning toast via keybind, and /warfront home). 5-second channel, broken by taking damage; units following the player come along; once per raid, free. After the raid, normal travel only.
If the player stays away, the raid still attacks: towers, guards and patrols defend alone (existing AI). Raiders still break blocks only if raidersBreakBlocks is on.
Test Panel: set preset, skip grace period, force a raid warning now, test recall.
Game tests: preset multipliers apply to a spawned raid; no raid in the grace period; recall moves the player and following units to the War Standard and only once per raid.

items.title: Daily loop, part 1: Mess Hall food upkeep and the worker economy
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: light food upkeep, advisor bounties, raid-the-raiders camps, a fuller worker economy and a neutral traveling merchant.
spec: Mess Hall: a base block with a large inventory (like a double chest) on the base's network area. Accepts any item in the vanilla/conventional food tags (c:foods), so other mods' crops count.

Once per in-game day (dawn) each battle unit within base range eats one food point budget (config, about 4 food points per unit) from the Mess Hall. Fed units get a 'Well Fed' morale bonus until next dawn: +10% resistance to routing and slow out-of-combat regen. Unfed units just don't get it. Never damage, desertion or death. Units away with the player eat when they return. Workers don't eat.
Farmers (FarmerGoal): also harvest grown Manabloom shards into the nearest Mana Well or chest, and deliver food to the Mess Hall before other chests.
Builders (BuilderGoal): after a raid, repair raid damage first (blocks broken by raiders, logged during the raid), then their normal blueprint work. Repairs use blocks from base chests, as now.
HUD / War Table: Mess Hall stock in days of food; toast at dawn if the troops went hungry.
Test Panel: controls for each part (fill/empty the Mess Hall, new bounties now, spawn a raider camp, summon the merchant).
Game tests: units in range get Well Fed when the Mess Hall has food and don't when it's empty; a farmer delivers food to the Mess Hall; builders rebuild a raider-broken block.

items.title: Daily loop, part 2: advisor bounties and raider camps
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: light food upkeep, advisor bounties, raid-the-raiders camps, a fuller worker economy and a neutral traveling merchant.
spec: Bounties: each dawn the advisor offers up to 3 (talk to him or the War Table). Types: clear a raider camp; scout a marked location (reach it); deliver materials (a stack of logs, iron, food...); rescue a captured unit (a bound friendly unit in a small camp, freed by right-click after clearing guards). Rewards: Mana Shards/Crystals and veterancy XP for the units that took part. Unfinished bounties expire after 2 days.

Raider camps: small enemy camps (tents, a fire, 4-8 raiders of one faction) spawn 100-300 blocks from the base, one every couple of days, each tied to the next scheduled raid of that faction. Taking the camp (all raiders beaten) shrinks that raid by about a third and drops part of its loot. Camps not taken in 3 days disband into their raid.
Camps fill the war meter like a beaten raid (half a point).
Test Panel: controls for each part (fill/empty the Mess Hall, new bounties now, spawn a raider camp, summon the merchant).
Game tests: a beaten camp lowers its linked raid's size; a delivered bounty pays out; bounties expire.

items.title: Daily loop, part 3: the traveling merchant
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: light food upkeep, advisor bounties, raid-the-raiders camps, a fuller worker economy and a neutral traveling merchant.
spec: A neutral caravan (merchant plus a pack beast and 2 guards) visits the player's War Standard every 3-5 days, stays one day, then leaves. Arrival toast. Never during a raid.

Trades (villager-style trade screen, themed later): sells rare materials (other races' building blocks, echo shards, Aether bits when present), beast eggs/summon tokens (still bound by beastLimit), spell scrolls when Iron's Spells is loaded, Manabloom seeds; buys raid loot and faction trophies; currency is Mana Crystals.
Stock rotates each visit; a couple of trades scale with base level.
Attacking the merchant makes him leave and skip the next visit.
Test Panel: controls for each part (fill/empty the Mess Hall, new bounties now, spawn a raider camp, summon the merchant).
Game tests: the merchant arrives on schedule and not during a raid; a trade exchanges items.

items.title: Mortal units, fallen heroes
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: units are mortal; heroes fall and can be revived.
spec: Basic troops and workers (every role except CAPTAIN, CHAMPION, BEAST) die for good, as now.

Player-owned Captains, Champions and war beasts don't die: at lethal damage they fall instead (cancel the death, health to 1, a FALLEN state synced to the client so they lie down; raiders' heroes still die).
While fallen: no AI or attacks, untargetable by enemies, can't be hurt; the owner sees a chat line saying where it fell. Window: 60 seconds (config).
Owner right-clicks a fallen hero within the window: it gets up at 50% health, with a short sound and particle cue.

Window runs out: the hero leaves the world and goes on its owner's 'returning heroes' list (a player attachment: role, race, tier, ready time). After 5 minutes (config) the owner can re-summon it at any of their altars for 50% of its mana cost; the altar menu shows returning heroes with a countdown.
Returning heroes still count toward beastLimit and the army cap, so they can't be dodged by letting heroes fall.

Game tests: a Champion at lethal damage falls instead of dying; a fallen hero is revived by its owner at half health; an expired hero lands on the returning list and is summoned at half cost; a Footman still dies.

items.title: Veterancy: 5 ranks with armor upgrades and insignia
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: 5 ranks with a slow climb, small stat boost per rank, upgraded armor tier and rank insignia.
spec: Applies to battle units (every role except Farmer, Builder and the retired Guard), heroes and war beasts included. Workers don't rank.
Ranks: 0 Recruit, 1 Regular, 2 Veteran, 3 Elite, 4 Legend. XP stored on the unit (saved to NBT, synced to the client for rendering).

XP: a kill gives XP equal to the victim's max health / 2 (min 1); surviving a won siege wave within range of the War Standard gives 25. Thresholds 100 / 300 / 700 / 1500 (config), so Legend takes many fights.

Bonuses, as permanent attribute modifiers with fixed ids per rank: +10% max health and +10% attack damage per rank (config), so Legend is +40%. Elite and Legend units never rout (hook into the existing rout check, same as frenzied orcs). Ranged units use the damage bonus on their projectiles.
Death: rank-and-file troops lose everything (they're gone). Fallen heroes (fallen-heroes item) keep rank and XP through revive and altar return; store it on the returning-heroes entry.

Armor look, one tier per rank, in the unit's race colors: Recruit as now; Regular gains leather/padded pieces; Veteran chain or iron pieces; Elite full plate; Legend plate with gold or race-colored trim. Built as generated texture overlays/armor layers from the generators (units.py / generate_assets.py), not hand-edited. Hive and imps get chitin or harness plating instead of metal.
Insignia: one chevron per rank on the shoulder (0 to 4), race-colored, as a small render layer.
Feedback: a rank-up gives a short particle burst and sound, plus a chat line for the owner ('Your Footman is now a Veteran'). The unit's name shows the rank title when it has one.
Codex: render one unit per race at all 5 ranks side by side.
Game tests: kills raise XP and rank at the threshold; health and damage modifiers match the rank; an Elite unit doesn't rout; a revived hero keeps its rank.

items.title: UI foundation: race-tinted theme, toasts and the siege banner
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: clean dark race-tinted panels; first pass is the combat HUD, War Table, base mana overlay and Altar redesign; toasts and a siege banner replace chat.
spec: A small theme library (client/ui/WFTheme + helpers): panel (semi-transparent near-black fill, 1px light border, optional accent top stripe), header text, bar (fill + track), icon slot, button; one accent color per race (Human steel blue, Elf leaf green, Dwarf bronze, Orc blood red, Demon ember orange, Angel gold, Hive cyan). All sizes respect the GUI scale; text uses the vanilla font with shadow off on panels.
Toasts (vanilla Toast API, styled with the theme): rank-up, hero fallen / revived / ready at the altar, mana network low or empty, beast limit reached. Duration about 4 seconds, stacked.

Siege banner: a wide centered banner near the top for wave start, wave won, outpost raised, outpost destroyed and War Standard lost; slides in, holds 3 seconds, fades. Race-tinted to the enemy faction.

Move the 26 current chat messages (Souls, Rage, GameEvents, AltarSummonPayload, ManaPylon/ManaWell blocks, WarStandard, SummoningAltar, CommanderBaton, WarHorn, SoldierEntity) to toasts, the banner, or the action bar for short feedback; keep chat for command output (WFCommands) only. A client config option 'chatAlerts' turns the old chat lines back on.
Game tests: the server sends the right alert payload for a rank-up, a fallen hero and a wave start (assert on a captured payload, not on rendering).

items.title: Rank ladder: bigger Captains and Champions
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: sizes follow rank, not role.
spec: In SoldierEntity's attribute setup, add a 'captain_scale' SCALE modifier of +0.15 (ADD_MULTIPLIED_BASE) for the CAPTAIN role, on top of unit_scale and race size.
Set champion_scale to +0.30 for every race except the Hive (keeps +0.35). Today it is 0.10 (0.15 orc/dwarf), so most Champions grow.
Other roles: no change. Warlord scale (0.45) unchanged.
Applies to raider heroes too, so enemy Captains and Champions are easy to spot.
Game test: a Captain's SCALE attribute is 1.15× a same-race soldier's, a Champion's 1.30×.
Render a race lineup (soldier, Captain, Champion) for the Codex.

items.title: Demon hellknights: Hellguard, Fiend, Archfiend, Hellknight, Blood Witch
spec: Generated in mods/warfront/tools/units.py like the imps, on the demon rig (no wings).
Shared look: faceless black-iron plate; horns breaking through the helm; digitigrade legs ending in hooves; emissive ember-orange in the visor slit and plate seams.
Hellguard: heaviest plate + tower shield. Fiend: plate + blade. Archfiend (Captain): crest or banner, cape. Hellknight (Champion): most ornate, bigger horns. Sizes from the rank ladder.
Blood Witch (healer): blood-red robes over light pauldrons, horned hood, no full plate.
Render the five beside a Black Legion soldier to prove they read as demons; set designs.json status to review.
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: armored hellknights with horns, hooves and ember seams; Blood Witch robed over light plate.

items.title: Enemy faction trim
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: same bodies, one signature trim piece per enemy faction (the pieces below are Claude's proposal under that decision; the owner can swap any at review).
spec: Add an overlay layer for raider soldiers keyed by NpcFaction (generated in mods/warfront/tools like worker gear), drawn on top of the race model and armor.
Marauder Horde (orc): war paint stripes and bone trophies on the belt and shoulders.
Black Legion (human): a black tabard with a white skull and a spiked pauldron.
Burning Horde (demon): smoldering chains and a soot-blackened brand on the chest.
The Swarm (Hive): glowing acid sacs on the back and jagged black chitin spurs.
Silverwood Reavers (elf): thorn-vine wraps and a pale antler-bone mask.
Ironbeard Clan (dwarf): a rune-etched iron face guard and braided beard rings.
Fallen Host (angel): torn, ash-gray wings and a cracked, dimmed halo.
Player-owned units never wear it. Keep it cosmetic: no stat changes.

items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: every 5th wave, scales with the wave, spawns raiders until taken, one raid chest per enemy faction.
items.title: Siege outposts and the raid chest
spec: Every 5th siege wave at a War Standard (5, 10, 15...) raises an outpost of the attacking NpcFaction 30 to 50 blocks from the standard, on solid ground, out of the base's tower reach where possible. Make the interval a config (default 5).
While the outpost stands the wave can't be won: the standard's wave-won check waits on it, and the siege bar or chat says 'Destroy the enemy outpost'.

Size scales with the wave: below wave 10, a watchtower camp (palisade ring, tent, wooden watchtower, campfire, about 11x11); from wave 10, a small fort (stone or faction-material walls, gate, two corner towers, about 17x17). Built from structure templates per faction palette; record every placed block so the outpost can be removed cleanly.
Pressure: the outpost sends a small group of its faction's raiders at the base every 90 seconds (config) until taken. It has a few guards of its own.

Raid chest: a new large block entity (2x2 footprint or a big single-block model) at the outpost's heart, with one look per NpcFaction: Marauder war crate, Black Legion strongbox, Burning Horde bone chest, Swarm chitin pod, Silverwood root-bound coffer, Ironbeard vault, Fallen Host reliquary. Holds loot scaled to the wave (loot table per faction). Can't be broken while it still holds items; once empty, breaking it despawns the whole outpost (all recorded blocks and remaining outpost raiders) with a sound and particles, and the wave can then be won.
If the siege ends some other way (the standard is lost or removed), the outpost despawns after a short delay so no ruins are left behind.

Game tests: an outpost spawns on wave 5 and not on wave 4; the wave can't be won while the chest stands; breaking the empty chest removes every outpost block; the chest can't be broken while it holds loot.
Models: render all seven chests side by side for the Codex before calling it done.

items.title: Campaign, part 1: random mixed raids and war meters
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: campaign endgame. Random mixed raids start wars; beating a faction's raids opens its warlord's fortress in its homeland; you march on it; own race's renegades last; then the hidden warlord behind the wars. Rewards: base trophy, warlord gear, Warlord title.
spec: Raids pick their faction at random, weighted so it stays mixed (no faction more than about 3 times in a row; factions not seen for a while get more likely). The player's own race's renegades only start raiding after the other six warlords are beaten.

War meter per player per faction (player attachment, saved): +1 per raid of that faction beaten (all raiders dead or routed near your base). At 5 (config) with base level 3+, the last raider of the next beaten raid drops that faction's War Map. Meters show in the War Table later (ui-war-table) and in /wftest.
War Map item: a filled map pointing to the faction's fortress (vanilla explorer-map style, using the structure tag from campaign-fortresses), named for the faction.
Test Panel: set any meter, give any War Map, mark warlords beaten.
Game tests: beating a raid raises its faction's meter; the War Map drops only at the threshold and base level; renegades of your own race don't raid until six warlords are down.

items.title: Campaign, part 2: warlord fortresses in each homeland
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: campaign endgame. Random mixed raids start wars; beating a faction's raids opens its warlord's fortress in its homeland; you march on it; own race's renegades last; then the hidden warlord behind the wars. Rewards: base trophy, warlord gear, Warlord title.
spec: Seven structures (jigsaw or NBT templates generated by a script, not hand-made): Black Legion keep (plains), Silverwood Reaver grove (forest), Ironbeard hold (mountains), Marauder war camp (badlands), Burning Horde citadel (Nether), Fallen Host bastion (Aether if loaded, else high mountains), Swarm hive (Otherside if loaded, else deep dark). Rare, far apart; each in a structure tag for its War Map.

Each fortress: outer defenses manned by that faction's units and its race towers, an inner keep, and the warlord's arena. Defenders respawn slowly until the warlord falls, so bringing an army matters.
Placeholder looks from the faction palettes and trims; final looks can follow references later.
Test Panel: teleport to the nearest fortress of any faction; place a fortress in front of you in a test world.
Game tests: a fortress template places and its defenders spawn hostile to the player.

items.title: Campaign, part 3: the seven warlords and their rewards
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: campaign endgame. Random mixed raids start wars; beating a faction's raids opens its warlord's fortress in its homeland; you march on it; own race's renegades last; then the hidden warlord behind the wars. Rewards: base trophy, warlord gear, Warlord title.
spec: One boss entity per faction with a boss bar and 2-3 phases; until the owner designs them (open question in needs.json), each is the faction race's Champion scaled up (about 1.6x), with the faction trim and a signature attack drawn from the race power (Soul Burst, Frenzy, long shots, lightning, holy smite, burrow ambush, shield wall). The warlord also calls defenders at phase changes.
Defeat: the fortress defenders rout; the warlord drops its trophy banner and a unique warlord gear piece; the player's campaign record marks it beaten.

Trophy banner: placed within 8 blocks of your War Standard, it gives a small permanent aura to your units in base range (one different bonus per warlord, e.g. +5% damage, +5% health, faster mana regen). Max one of each.
Warlord gear: one unique weapon or armor piece per warlord, usable by any race, with a bonus tied to that faction's power.
Own race last: your own race's renegade warlord's War Map can only drop after the other six are beaten.
After all seven: grant the 'Warlord' title (shown in the player's name and the War Table) and drop the clue that opens the final boss (campaign-final-boss).
Game tests: beating a warlord records it, drops banner and gear; the trophy aura applies near the standard; the title appears after all seven.

items.title: Campaign, part 4: the hidden warlord (secretly the good guy)
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: campaign endgame. Random mixed raids start wars; beating a faction's raids opens its warlord's fortress in its homeland; you march on it; own race's renegades last; then the hidden warlord behind the wars. Rewards: base trophy, warlord gear, Warlord title. Owner, 2026-10-07: he is the advisor's brother; on defeat he dies and hands over his blade and the key to the End. Owner, 2026-10-07: his fortress is the frozen battlefield of the brothers' first war, a pocket dimension reached by joining the seven War Maps; the brothers share one face and build.
spec: Identity: the advisor's brother, same ancient power. He set the factions against the player to stop the advisor's chosen champion from rising.

On defeat he dies: a short dying scene (chat/toast-style lines) reveals the advisor is his brother and the true enemy, then drops his blade (unique weapon, any race) and the Key to the End, which triggers campaign-betrayal.

Fortress: a Warfront pocket dimension ('the Frozen Field'): a battlefield sealed out of time under a still, colorless sky, with stone statues of armies of all seven races caught mid-fight, broken siege engines and banners. Structures: outer field, a ruined war camp of mixed race styles, and his keep at the center. Fought there using every race's tricks across his phases; statues near him can wake up as defenders at phase changes.

Entry: after all seven warlords, combining the seven War Maps (crafting or right-click with all seven) makes the Sealed Map; using it at a War Standard opens a portal there. Your whole army can march through. Leaving or losing returns you home.

Look: same face and build as the advisor's true form, but scarred and armored. Until the owner designs them, use a stand-in: tall knight in worn, mismatched armor, a cracked crown, gray and faded gold.

items.title: Campaign, part 5: the betrayal and the fight in the End
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: one villain in seven disguises is each race's advisor, runs the tutorial, is revealed after the hidden warlord falls (who was trying to stop him), and is fought in the End with only your heroes and beasts against a mixed army.
spec: After the hidden warlord's dying reveal, the advisor appears, drops his disguise (short scene) and teleports the player to the End main island with only their Captains, Champions and war beasts (fallen or returning heroes come back for this fight). Rank-and-file troops stay home.
Compatibility: require the vanilla Ender Dragon to be beaten first (the End is then empty); the advisor's dragon is a Warfront 'bound dragon' entity, so the vanilla fight state isn't touched.
He holds the island with waves of mixed troops from all seven races and his own towers, in phases: army, towers and summons, then he mounts the bound dragon for the last phase.
Losing returns the player home (heroes fall as usual); the fight can be retried.
Victory: the End is freed, credits-style closing lines, a final trophy and the campaign marked complete.

items.title: Orc flight: the rocket pack
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: fuel-burst rocket, not long-haul flight.
spec: Chest-slot item, orc only. Hold jump in the air to thrust: upward when looking level or up, forward-and-up when looking down the sprint direction. Strong acceleration, capped speed.

Burns fuel fast: about 3 seconds of thrust per coal/charcoal, about 8 per Mana Crystal (config). Fuel sits in the pack (right-click with fuel to load, tooltip shows seconds left). Empty pack = falls like normal.
Loud and visible: smoke and flame particles plus a rocket sound while thrusting, so enemies hear orcs coming.
Landing from a dive within a second of thrusting does a small knockback shockwave and cancels the orc's fall damage; no damage to blocks.
Placeholder look: a plain iron-and-copper pack on the back with two exhausts (generated, like the glider model); the real design waits on orc player references.
Same pattern as the Mana Glider (flight/ManaGliderItem.java): race-locked, chest-slot or ability as noted, vanilla attributes/effects where possible, a game test for the race lock and the cost.

items.title: Angel flight: wings that fly by day and glide by night
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: free flight by day, elytra glide at night or underground.
spec: Angel players get wings (chest-slot item until the angel player model has built-in wings). Daytime with open sky above (world can see sky at the player's position, not raining hard): creative-style free flight (mayfly), with a slower top speed than creative.
Night, underground, or no sky: flight shuts off and the wings act as an elytra glide only. Switching mid-air drops the player into the glide, never a straight fall.
Crafting: the fallback vanilla recipe now (feathers, Mana Crystals, gold); the Aether recipe from the crossover item replaces it when the Aether is loaded.
Placeholder look: plain white feathered wings from a generated model; the real look waits on the angel player references.
Game test: an angel with wings can fly in daylight with sky and can't (glide only) under a roof.
Same pattern as the Mana Glider (flight/ManaGliderItem.java): race-locked, chest-slot or ability as noted, vanilla attributes/effects where possible, a game test for the race lock and the cost.

items.title: Elf flight: levitate and wind leap spells
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: spell flight paid with Iron's Spells mana.
spec: Two elf-only spells. Levitate: hover and drift slowly while held, a steady mana drain. Wind Leap: a burst launch in the look direction plus slow fall until landing, one cost per cast.
With Iron's Spells loaded: register them as Iron's Spells spells (elf school or nature), paid from Iron's mana, on spell scrolls/ink like the mod's own.
Without Iron's Spells: a Wind Charm item (elf only) casts them, paid with Mana Shards from the inventory. Warfront must load and pass tests without Iron's Spells.
Leaf and wind particles; no wings, no gear on the back.
Same pattern as the Mana Glider (flight/ManaGliderItem.java): race-locked, chest-slot or ability as noted, vanilla attributes/effects where possible, a game test for the race lock and the cost.

items.title: Dwarf tunnels: rune drill, rune stone and tunnel traps
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: dwarves tunnel instead of flying; drill plus reinforced tunnels; spike floor, rune mine and flame vent traps.
spec: Rune Drill (dwarf only, tool item): mines a 3x3 face per use at pickaxe tiers up to diamond, faster than a pickaxe; uses durability, repaired with Mana Crystals. Won't break blocks with a block entity or rune stone. Non-dwarves get a 'too heavy' message.

Rune Stone (block, plus stairs/slab/wall): crafted from stone or deepslate + Mana Shards. Very high blast resistance (like obsidian or more) and slow to mine for anyone but a dwarf with a Rune Drill or pickaxe (break-speed event). Enemy raiders and Swarm tunnelers can't dig through it; add it to a warfront:raider_unbreakable tag the raid AI checks.

Spike Floor (block): looks like a plain floor; when a hostile or enemy-faction mob steps on it, spikes pop up for 6 damage and a short slow, then reset after 2 seconds. Never hits the owner, their units or allies. Reusable.

Rune Mine (block): hidden in the floor, triggers on enemies only (same friend check), explodes for heavy damage in a small radius without breaking blocks, then is consumed. Crafted with a Mana Crystal.
Flame Vent (block): joins the base mana network like a tower; when an enemy is within 8 blocks in the direction it faces, it sprays fire for a few seconds and draws mana per burst. No mana, no fire.
Friend-or-foe check shared with towers (reuse the tower targeting rules).

Game tests: Rune Drill digs 3x3 and only for dwarves; spike floor hurts an enemy and not an owned unit; rune mine triggers once and leaves blocks intact; flame vent fires only with mana; raid AI won't break rune stone.

items.title: Dwarf identity: Hold the Line, mountain hold start, deep miners
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: dwarves get Hold the Line (Resolve meter and Oath of Stone) as their race power, start at a mountain hold gate, and are deep miners (more crystals, faster stone mining, fewer Manabloom shards).
spec: Hold the Line, Resolve 0-100 (a player attachment, synced; same pattern as demon souls and orc rage). Gain while in combat (hit or got hit in the last 3 s): +4 per second while not sprinting, +6 per hit taken. Sprinting loses 10 per second; out of combat for 4 s it drains 10 per second.
Resolve bonus through vanilla attributes (transient modifiers): +1 armor and +5% knockback resistance per 20 Resolve (max +5 armor, +25%).

Oath of Stone: at 100 Resolve, crouching triggers it (spends all Resolve). For 6 s: +80% knockback resistance, 30% less damage taken, Slowness I. When it ends, a stone shockwave: 4 damage and a strong knockback to enemies within 4 blocks, block-particle burst and an anvil/stone sound.
Dwarf soldiers build Resolve the same way and swear the Oath automatically at 100; they don't rout while it lasts.

Mountain hold start: when a player first picks dwarf, find the nearest mountain biome (tag #minecraft:is_mountain, search a bounded radius around spawn) and place a small hold-gate structure in the slope (carved stone gate, braziers, a 3x3 starter tunnel about 12 blocks long, a starter chest), then move the player there and set their respawn. No mountain found: fall back to normal spawn. Reuse the Hive cave-start code path.

Deep miners: breaking Mana Ore as a dwarf has a 50% chance of +1 Mana Crystal (stacks with Fortune); dwarves mine blocks in #minecraft:base_stone_overworld and deepslate 20% faster (break-speed event, so other mods' tools still work); Manabloom harvested by a dwarf gives 20% fewer shards (rounded, minimum 1).
HUD: Resolve meter in the race-power slot (stone-gray, glows when the Oath is ready). Test Panel and /wftest: fill or empty Resolve, trigger the Oath, place a hold gate here.

Game tests: Resolve rises in combat and drains out of it; the Oath fires at 100 and the shockwave knocks back a nearby enemy; dwarf Mana Ore drops average above other races; armor modifier applied and removed.

items.title: Race towers, wave 1: the system plus the seven level 2 towers
items.decided: Owner, 2026-10-07: 3 race towers per race (base level 2, 3, 5), own race only, race towers capped by base level, capstones 1 each.
spec: System: a RaceTower base (block + block entity) with race, unlock level and cap group. Placement checks: placer's race matches, the base on that mana network is at the unlock level, and the race-tower cap isn't reached (2/4/6/10 for base levels 2-5; capstones max 1 each). Refuse with a toast (ui-foundation) or action-bar message saying why.
Count placed race towers per base (stored with the base data); breaking one frees the slot. Losing base level doesn't remove towers, but blocks new ones over the cap.
Human: Ballista: long-range bolt that pierces a line of enemies; bonus damage to beasts and large mobs.
Elf: Thornwood Sentinel: roots the nearest enemies in vines (heavy slow, short root) and marks them Glowing so archers focus them.
Dwarf: Rune Cannon: slow heavy shot, splash damage on impact, no block damage.
Orc: War Drum Totem: support: orc units within 12 blocks gain Rage faster; each drum beat has a chance to make nearby enemies flee briefly.
Demon: Soul Pyre: sets enemies on fire; kills near it charge it, and at 10 charges it unleashes a fire burst.
Angel: Sun Lance: holy beam; strong by day with open sky, weak at night; bonus damage to demons, Hive and undead.
Hive: Lurker Pit: hidden in the ground until enemies come close, then ambushes with acid that lowers armor; stronger underground.

Every race tower is a block entity on the base mana network like the existing towers (draws mana per shot or pulse; no mana, no effect) and reuses the tower friend-or-foe targeting. Placeholder models are generated and styled in the race palette, following the tower-models item; final looks can follow references later. Numbers live in config. Codex: a render and a one-line description per tower.
Game tests: wrong race can't place; under-level base can't place; cap enforced; each tower acts only with mana; one effect test per tower (assert on a counter or state).
